newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK home prices to cool if gov't acts - M. Stanley.
newsitem.headline: HK home prices to cool if gov't acts - M. Stanley.

text.p: The booming Hong Kong residential property market would cool by year-end if the government enacts anti-speculation measures, Peter Churchouse, managing director at Morgan Stanley Asia, said on Wednesday.
"I don't think there is going to be a big adjustment, but I think it could see some adjustment," Churchhouse said.

Churchouse predicted that average home prices would be up just 15-20 percent by year-end 1997 over year-end 1996 if measures are taken. At present, home prices are 30 percent higher than at the end of last year, he said.

C.Y. Leung, a property surveyor named by future leader Tung Chee-hwa as head of a post-colonial committee to map out long-term housing strategy, has completed a report on the subject but details have not been released.
Churchouse said he would be surprised if the government introduced a new type of tax to curb property speculation. He said authorities are more likely to increase existing taxes, such as stamp taxes.
He also said he expected the government to increase land supply.
Any measures to curb speculation are unlikely to have the same dramatic effect as in 1994, when the government also took aim at the problem of soaring property prices, Churchouse said.
In 1994, prices fell 25 to 30 percent. Churchouse said prices were unlikely to fall as much in 1997 because Hong Kong's economy is better now.
